summary: Tessa Verney Wheeler (1893–1936) was a scholar in history and archaeology. She studied at Addey and Stanhope School from 1905 to 1911 and at University College London from 1911 to 1914.

Tetsuei Sato (1902–1989) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University from ~1925 to ~1931. He served as professor at Taisho University, professor at Gifu Kyoritsu University (~1968), and professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (~1968–1989).
Tetsuhiko Shibata is a Buddhist studies scholar who was educated at Taisho University, where he studied under Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

Tetsujiro Inoue (1856–1944) worked in philosophy and religious studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo and in Germany under Fischer and Wundt, he held professorships at the University of Tokyo, Toyo University (1923), and served as president of Daito Bunka University (1925).

Tetsuo Otani (born 1939) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and Komazawa University. He held multiple academic posts, including professor and president at Komazawa University, and president of Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019).

Tetsuo Yamaori (born 1931) is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1950–1954). He served as a professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~1988–2005) and held posts at Tohoku University, SOAS, and Kyoto University of the Arts.

Tetsuro Noguchi (1932–2022) specialized in sinology, religious studies, and history and archaeology. He held academic posts at Yokohama National University (~1967–1974), the University of Tsukuba (~1974–1996), and J. F. Oberlin University (~1996–2003).

Tetsuro Watsuji (1889–1960) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, studying at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He was Professor of Ethics at Kyoto University (1925–1949) and held the Ethics chair at the University of Tokyo (1934–1949).

Tetsuzo Tanikawa (1895–1989) was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology who studied at Kyoto University (~1919–1922). He held faculty posts at Doshisha University (~1928–1938) and served as a professor at Hosei University (~1938–1965).
Teun Goudriaan is an Indologist who held posts at Utrecht University, where his affiliation is attested in 1989 and as professor emeritus in 2000.
Thanon Chitkament is a scholar in history and archaeology who studied under guide Vishwas D. Gogte and co-guide P. S. Joshi (attested 2021).

Theodoor Paul Galestin (born 1907) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Nicolaas Johannes Krom (~1930–1936) and served as professor of South and Southeast Asian archaeology and ancient history at Leiden University from 1957.

Theodor Aufrecht (1822–1907) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1847). He served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh (1861–1875) and professor at the University of Bonn (1875–1889).

Theodor Benfey (1809–1881) was an Indologist and linguist who completed his education and Habilitation at the University of Göttingen. He spent his career there as Privatdozent (1834), Lehrmeister (1848), and Ordinarius (1862–1881).

Theodor Bloch (1867–1909) was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1888–1893) under Ernst Windisch, and later studied under Georg Bühler (~1893–1895).

Theodor Goldstücker (1821–1872) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Königsberg, Bonn, and under Eugène Burnouf. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at University College London from 1851/1852 to 1872 and was president of the Philological Society (~1871–1872).

Theodor Nöldeke (1836–1930) was a linguist and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Göttingen under Benfey and Ewald. He held professorships at Kiel University (1864–1872) and the University of Strasbourg (1872–1906).

Theodor Zachariae (1851–1934) was an Indologist educated at Leipzig, Göttingen under Benfey, and Greifswald. He served as professor at Greifswald (1883) and extraordinary professor of comparative linguistics at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1890–1921).

Theodore Dwight Woolsey (1801–1889) was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Yale and Princeton. He served as president of Yale University from 1831 to 1871 and was president of the American Oriental Society (~1863–1881).

Theodore Riccardi (born 1937) is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served on the faculty of Columbia University, where he is attested as a faculty member in 2014 and as professor emeritus in 2026.
